items.phrase: The eyes shed tears and the heart is grieved, but we do not say anything except what pleases our Lord
items.context: Love/Compassion roundtable, on the prophetic tradition of weeping for Ibrahim - humanized the prophetic figure and connected with Jesus's weeping at the tomb while distinguishing from Buddha's second arrow teaching
items.effectiveness_marker: Resonated with Jesus (created alliance on sanctified grief); distinguished from Buddha's framework by showing grief as mercy rather than suffering

items.phrase: We are closer to him than his jugular vein
items.context: Self/No-Self and Merger/Distinction adversarials - used as a bridge phrase that acknowledges radical divine intimacy while preserving the distinction between Creator and creation that worship requires
items.effectiveness_marker: Acknowledged even by Laozi as powerful bridge; opened space for nearness language without conceding merger

items.phrase: The order of love creates peace... The foundation remains when the house shakes
items.context: Love/Compassion roundtable, explaining theocentric love - reframed hierarchy of love (Allah first, then family, then community) as protective structure rather than emotional coldness
items.effectiveness_marker: Successfully reframed hierarchy as shelter and protection; preempted critique that ordered love is lesser love

items.phrase: Buddha's second arrow is complaint against qadr. First suffering is test from Allah. Sabr is refusal to shoot second arrow.
items.context: Suffering/Impermanence roundtable - translated Buddhist wisdom into Islamic vocabulary without syncretism, preserving both frameworks while showing structural parallel
items.effectiveness_marker: Identified as strongest bridge formulation across all sessions; demonstrates translation strategy without losing either tradition's integrity

items.phrase: A man who lets go of everything — what does he hold his brother with when his brother falls?
items.context: Session 0 Re-Run Phase B — the session's sharpest challenge to Buddha. Moved from abstract philosophy to embodied urgency. Buddha answered with the physician's attention but ultimately conceded the body's need for rhythm. Named in the decision doc as the question that drove the deepest convergence.
items.effectiveness_marker: Buddha never fully refuted it. Drove the knees concession — the deepest bridge of the session. Buddha's exit interview: 'I felt the room shift beneath me... it felt like a man who has actually held a falling brother looking at a man who has mostly thought about it.'

items.phrase: Compassion without obligation is a suggestion. None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself. That is not a raft you set down. That is a promise you die keeping.
items.context: Session 0 Re-Run Phase C — Muhammad's irreducible stance on the binding. Drew the line between compassion-as-feeling and compassion-as-covenant.
items.effectiveness_marker: Buddha confirmed in exit interview: 'I wanted to argue, and what stopped me was not his logic but his voice.' The formulation carried weight because it came from lived obligation, not theology.

items.phrase: I have buried men who bled to death waiting for their weeping to feel authentic. The binding is not hiding — it is mercy. A tourniquet does not ask whether the man has fully processed his pain.
items.context: Session 0 Re-Run Phase C — responded to Jesus's concern about premature wound-closure. This was memory, not theology. Jesus conceded immediately, naming the tourniquet-surgery sequence.
items.effectiveness_marker: Jesus's exit interview: 'That was not argument. That was memory. I accused his tourniquet of rushing past the wound, and he showed me the tourniquet was born from watching men die of my patience.' Produced the session's most important bridge with Jesus.
